messages.subject: Huge standard error?
parts:
Dear Phil,

I analyzed a three-item dichotomous test under the 2PL model with mirt. I noticed that one of the items has a really huge standard error and I was wondering is this something that would be considered usual, or is it more plausible to think that there was some sort of an error in the estimation due to the small number of items? Unfortunately I cannot post raw data here since it's confidential, but I am happy to provide more information that would be necessary. This is the plot of the item information/SE curves.

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Huge standard error?
parts:
This has more to do with the fact that you have a discrimination parameter tending to infinity. It's generally a sign of estimation problems since step-functions are generally deterred in IRT models (they become equal to Guttman steps), and so the concept of 'discrimination' fails because the item can perfectly discriminate individuals above and below the threshold. You could put a prior on the discrimination to keep this away from infinity in case you think this is unreasonable. HTH.

Phil

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Huge standard error?
parts:
For your situation I would imagine a log-normal prior would be okay. But no I don't really know of guidelines for priors (and even if I didn't, wouldn't recommend them since their purpose is to include "prior belief" about the distribution of the parameters). 

Phil
